notes:
After Create a user or New staff, the result window shows the password with a Copy button. It then offers the usual follow-ups: open the person, print the account card (and the welcome sheet for New staff), add to a class, create another.
After Suspend from a table or the details panel, the pop-up has Next steps: move them, transfer their files, sign out everywhere.
Paste a list… appears next to every list of people and next to the Chromebook serial box.
People: paste emails, names, “Doe, John” or student IDs. GAMbit shows what it found, what it couldn’t match, and names that match more than one person, before anything is added.
Chromebooks: serials and asset tags are checked against the saved Chromebook list.
Row buttons: hovering a row in a people or Chromebook table shows small Open, Reset password and Sign out buttons (or Re-enable and Disable for Chromebooks) at its right end.
Changes today: in the bell menu or with Ctrl+Shift+Z. It lists today’s changes, optionally the whole team’s, each with Undo when GAMbit saved the earlier state.
Simple mode: turn it on in Settings & Updates → Appearance. Home becomes six big buttons:
reset a password
unlock
fix sign-in
print a card
find a Chromebook
ticket queue
Each button asks “who?” or “which Chromebook?” first. The sidebar shows only those pages, and Leave simple mode in the top bar turns it off.
Jargon help: a small ⓘ after labels like Org unit, License and Asset ID explains the term in one sentence. Table headings do the same on hover.
Run tonight at 6 PM is on the big-change confirmation. The change goes into Run later & freezes and nothing changes now. It runs from GAMbit’s existing background task, so that task needs to be set up on that PC (Schedules → Setup & health).
Saved views: from a table’s list button. A view keeps the filter, columns and sort, comes back from Saved views, and Add to Home pins it to Home favorites. If the table is empty, the view applies once you run the search.
Print or save as PDF is in the same menu. The printout includes your district, the page, the date and time, the filter used and the row count, and switches to landscape for wide tables.
Consistency pass on older pages. Many pages were built before the modern components, so a few probably still have old-style layouts, odd spacing, or a table without empty-state text or an org-unit box that’s still plain text. I’d go through every page and bring them in line.
Update the tour and the Guide. The “Take the tour” walkthrough and some Guide articles may still describe the old layout (the Domain label, the Output panel always open, Browse… buttons). New techs will follow them literally.
First-day checklist on Home. This is #10 from the last list: connect GAM, map schools, set a test account, try a dry run, pin your pages, each ticking itself off. It’s most useful when you roll GAMbit out to other techs.
District name setting. A box in Settings for “Hancock County Schools”, used on printouts, account cards, welcome sheets and the sidebar instead of the domain.
